messages:
toni: Heads-up: new hire ran into redwoodctl after brew install. Auth login says success but `redwoodctl samples run` complains about missing token. They have XDG_CONFIG_HOME set by their dotfiles.

rahul: can you paste `cat $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood/token` and `ls -la ~/.redwood`?

toni: token exists at ~/.config/redwood/token. ~/.redwood is empty. redwoodctl 2.3.1 (from brew).

pat: i've seen this. Installer (homebrew) writes creds using XDG, but CLI runtime still checks only ~/.redwood by default unless REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR is set. flaky parity.

toni: confirmed that `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood redwoodctl samples run` works. But we shouldn't require everyone to export env vars.

kira: quick fix: symlink `~/.config/redwood -> ~/.redwood` or run `redwoodctl auth login --config-dir ~/.redwood` to re-write. But long term: runtime should probe XDG first, then legacy dir.

rahul: opened issue and PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/1033 — "cli: prefer XDG_CONFIG_HOME then fallback to ~/.redwood; document behavior". Also adding a `redwoodctl doctor` suggestion to the PR that prints config locations and found tokens.

ci-bot: CI note: if we change config path behavior, update the homebrew formula postinstall step and the macOS quickstart note. Also add e2e test for `redwoodctl auth login` with XDG set.

pat: another edge case: some users have both token locations present with different tokens. Need clear precedence rules and a migration helper `redwoodctl migrate-config` to copy/link tokens. otherwise rollouts will confuse users.

toni: posting minimal repro and steps into the GH issue and tagging eng-cli + devex. Will keep the symlink for now. thanks all. :slightly_smiling_face:
